title: Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscriptions (CSP) Order Terms: Purchase, Unit Price, Term Dates and Cycle Charges
content:
## 1. Placing a subscription

1.1 A new Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscriptions (CSP) subscription is placed for one plan, a term listed among the plan's terms offered, and a billing frequency that term offers. A P1M term takes the P1M billing frequency. A P1Y or P3Y term takes one of the billing frequencies offered on P1Y and P3Y. The subscription must have at least the plan's fewest licenses per order.

1.2 A new subscription may be placed only from the authorized contact's signed order form. The evidence is the system record of a signed change request for the purchase. A statement that the form was signed is not enough.

1.3 Microsoft 365 F3 is the plan whose licenses are for frontline workers only. It may be assigned only to frontline workers who do not use a dedicated computer, and a request to license office staff on it is refused.

## 2. Unit price

2.1 The locked unit price depends on the term and billing frequency:

- for a P1Y or P3Y term billed annually, the plan's annual price;
- for a P1Y or P3Y term billed monthly, the annual price increased by the plan's monthly billing surcharge percentage;
- for a P1M term, the annual price increased by the plan's P1M premium percentage.

Each price is rounded half up to the cent.

2.2 Because the price is locked for the term, it stays fixed for the term and changes only at renewal or upgrade. Where the plan carries the three-year price lock, a P3Y term keeps the price for all three years.

2.3 A new subscription renews automatically unless the order form says otherwise, because auto-renew is on by default.

## 3. Term and billing cycles

3.1 The term starts on the purchase date. It ends the day before the same day of the month one month (P1M), twelve months (P1Y) or thirty-six months (P3Y) later. When that day does not exist in the end month, the last day of that month is used as the anniversary.

3.2 Billing cycles start on the term start date, and then on the same day of each following month for monthly billing or of each following year for annual billing. When the day does not exist, the last day of the month stands in. Each cycle ends the day before the next one starts.

3.3 Each cycle is invoiced on its first day. A monthly cycle is charged the unit price times the licenses held at the cycle start. An annual cycle is charged twelve times that. Both are rounded half up to the cent. The first cycle is invoiced when the subscription is provisioned.

3.4 A cycle charge may be invoiced only while the subscription status is active or suspended, as the subscription record shows.

## Worked figures (hypothetical annual price of 10.00 USD, 5 percent surcharge, 20 percent premium)

| Term and billing | Unit price | Cycle charge for 8 licenses |
|---|---|---|
| P1Y billed annually | 10.00 | 12 times 10.00 times 8, that is 960.00 per annual cycle |
| P1Y billed monthly | 10.50 | 10.50 times 8, that is 84.00 per monthly cycle |
| P1M | 12.00 | 12.00 times 8, that is 96.00 per monthly cycle |

A P1Y subscription purchased on 15 March has a term that ends on 14 March of the following year.
